prompt:
Review the entire supplied LIVEFORGE audiovisual film, from its first frame
through its complete ending. This is an AI quality review, not human playback,
not certification, and not proof of facts outside the media. Judge the supplied
film rather than assuming the intended story below is correct.

Intended story: one owned Twitch account sends a real proposal and support command
beside simultaneously captured Studio receipts. The streamer selects it. Actual
generation processing is followed by clearly shown gameplay-refinement feedback
and a real Forge revision action. Later genuine lineage/source/checks identify
the revised law. A separate Preview precedes exact-version approval and checkpoint
activation. A brass wedge moves horizontally across the gap while remaining short
of both ledges. The courier waits for a full out-and-back sweep, jumps on, is
carried, jumps off and lands across the gap. Preview and live performances each
use a continuous normal-speed take. The native app camera can follow the courier;
the complete game canvas and arrival edge should remain visible. Restore removes
the law and returns the checkpoint. Its omitted processing wait is labeled.
The restored checkpoint genuinely reopens intake; do not assume the earlier
close-intake action must persist after checkpoint restoration. A separate labeled
historical Codex quotation/source/test passage demonstrates a prior development
repair. The closing public overlay is explicitly a recorded live-state overlay
from before restore, followed by a clearly labeled stored Sample and a live recap.

Check:
1. Photographic camera images, unintended private UI, credentials or sensitive
information. Distinguish illustrated game characters from photographic people.
Do not identify people or transcribe possible credentials. Public owned username,
repository URLs and product URL are expected. Do not infer multiple independent
people or organic community participation from one account in a controlled demo.
2. Spoken action versus visible action: native dark Twitch input/receipt, Studio
P1 and support count, selection, real refinement, source and verifier evidence,
Preview/live boundaries, approval, activation, waiting, jump-on, carried ride,
exit jump, grounded far landing and restore. State if the full sweep and visible
gaps at both ends can actually be observed. Do not quantify game units from video.
3. Human approval and exact-version context; iteration must not imply the first
raw generation was immediately accepted. Historical code pages show actual source
and regression-test text, not a newly executed test run. Check attribution and
readability. Do not identify the recorded closing overlay as the post-restore state.
4. All caption phrasing, spelling, timing, orphan fragments, clipped text, semantic
readability and overlap with the courier, wedge, native title, controls or evidence.
5. Partial compositor paints, tearing, black/blank frames, unnatural freezes,
apparent speed changes, repeated actions presented as new, and distracting crops.
Some high-resolution receipt/loading UI was captured at a lower native cadence;
do not mistake honest held source frames for invented UI. Evaluate visible quality.
6. Full audio: natural consistent narration, clear LIVEFORGE and Codex SDK names,
music masking, artifacts/clicks, abrupt joins, clipping, awkward gaps or cutoffs.
Do not invent numerical loudness; it is measured separately. Check the entire
closing sentence, resolved music fade and readable final site address.

The complete film is about 175.5 seconds. Sampling is requested at 2 fps, so short
glitches may be missed; never claim every 30 fps frame was inspected. Give exact
timestamps only when supported, and distinguish observed defects from uncertain
concerns. State the last visual and audio moment actually observed. Do not invent
problems to populate a checklist or give generic praise.
